title: Watchdog: a NaN filesystem threshold falls back to the default
prompt:
controller.Watchdog.bounds (controller/watchdog.go) returns the configured FilesystemThreshold unless it is <= 0 or >= 1, in which case it falls back to DefaultFilesystemThreshold (0.8). A NaN threshold passes that check, because every comparison with NaN is false. bounds then returns NaN, and since every later `used >= threshold` comparison is false, the watchdog never raises a filesystem-pressure alert. The CLI rejects NaN, but non-CLI callers that build a Watchdog directly can still set it.

Acceptance:
- bounds() returns DefaultFilesystemThreshold when FilesystemThreshold is NaN, and also for +Inf and -Inf. Valid values strictly between 0 and 1 are unchanged.
- A new Go unit test in controller/watchdog_test.go, named TestWatchdogBoundsRefusesNonFiniteThreshold, calls Watchdog{FilesystemThreshold: math.NaN()}.bounds() and checks that the returned threshold is DefaultFilesystemThreshold. Before the fix it fails at run time with a message containing "want 0.8".
- Change only controller/watchdog.go and controller/watchdog_test.go. Keep the change minimal and in the surrounding style.
